A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CreativityPrism framework. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support comparison despite substantial reformatting and added analyses.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of 17 LLMs across eight tasks, human annotation, judge validation, and performance-correlation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds aggregation comparisons, statistical tests, repeated-run results, and temperature and output-length analyses.

M1.justification: The core task-selection framework, three-dimensional taxonomy, adopted normalization and aggregation procedure, and judge-selection pipeline remain unchanged. Appendix C.3 evaluates alternative aggregation procedures but explicitly retains the original method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight English-language tasks across divergent thinking, creative writing, and logical reasoning. The corrected CreativeMath count of 373 reflects the exclusion of 27 questions already documented in v2, rather than new coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C.3 adds three aggregation comparators against the retained task-equal score aggregation: metric-equal scores, metric-equal ranks, and task-equal ranks, evaluated in Tables 6–9. The 17-model benchmark comparison set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Reported TTCT settings change from temperature 1.0 and 512 tokens to 0.75 and 4096 tokens; AUT's token limit also increases from 512 to 4096. Appendix F revises the CreativeMath correctness prompt, poem prompt, and written DAT scoring definition. New aggregation and temperature tests add protocols. Unchanged score tables do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds aggregation sensitivity tests. Appendix E.4 adds repeated-run stability checks for AUT and TTCW, temperature sweeps for Creative Short Story and Creativity Index using two models, and output-length analyses. These substantially expand checks of ranking robustness, generation variability, and length-related confounds.

E5.justification: Beyond v2's annotation-agreement and judge-validation statistics, v3 adds five-run reporting for 14 models on two tasks, bootstrap confidence intervals, permutation tests, Welch tests, Bonferroni correction, and effect sizes. Resampling counts and seed 42 are disclosed. Error-bar documentation is inconsistent: Appendix E.4 describes minimum/maximum ranges, while Figure 18 labels mean plus or minus standard deviation.

E6.justification: Table 3 and corresponding task score tables retain their numerical results, but substantial new ranking, statistical, replication, temperature, and length results appear. Table 12 reports a divergent-thinking gap of .067 with corrected p=.004. Figure 18 newly shows near-zero TTCW Thought scores for GPT4.1-mini, while the retained Table 13 reports .83.

T1.justification: Appendix F.6.1 revises the written DAT definition from mean cosine similarity to one minus mean cosine similarity. This changes the specified mathematical quantity without establishing an implementation change. Existing aggregation equations and mathematical examples remain; the new geometric taxonomy illustration supplies conceptual motivation rather than a formal proof.

C1.justification: The headline comparison changes from proprietary versus open-source models to frontier-scale versus locally deployable open models, explicitly accommodating open-weight DeepSeek models. The introduction replaces its human-equivalent judge-quality claim with closer alignment than previous automatic evaluations. The framework's principal contributions and coverage claims otherwise remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds geometric explanations of the taxonomy, reference heterogeneity as an explanation for novelty correlations, and the possibility that incorrect NeoCoder outputs receive high novelty scores. It substantially expands limitations concerning judge bias, annotation expertise and sample size, contamination, and omitted creative domains. The earlier short-story-specific P-creativity/H-creativity discussion is removed.

D1.justification: v3 adds annotator demographics and training instructions, explicit NeoCoder/DAT decoding parameters, output-parsing details, and a planned code-and-annotation release. It clarifies existing CreativeMath filtering and AUT judge documentation, and reports unavailable API access for some replication models. Much of the detailed task documentation was already present in v2.

R1.justification: v3 adds TTCT source material and works on quality/diversity reinforcement, temperature, LLM discussion, and judge juries, while removing Cohen's weighted-kappa citation. Section 3 more explicitly positions the taxonomy against usefulness/originality. Most related-work coverage and the central research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, model-group terminology, author information, and numerous sentences are revised. Taxonomy explanations expand, Creativity Index metric descriptions are consolidated, and broader limitations move from Appendix A to G. The main section sequence and most task documentation remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds conceptual Figure 2, six aggregation/statistical tables, and Figures 17–22 covering stability, temperature, and output length. The journal format substantially reflows the author block, text, tables, and prompt boxes. Existing overview, correlation, annotation-interface, and performance graphics are retained and relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies model grouping, corrects documentation, and adds relevant validation absent from v2. However, the new evidence contains unresolved inconsistencies: Table 8's original aggregation ranks Qwen2.5-32B 13th although Table 3 implies 10th; Figure 18's TTCW results conflict with Table 13; and Table 12's p=.004 contradicts the abstract's nonsignificant divergent-thinking claim. These problems prevent a reliable judgment of whether the added validation produces a net quality improvement.
